description: This bar chart, from the paper “An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment of COVID-19 vaccines,” illustrates the distribution of tweets based on the number of labels assigned to them, with the vertical axis labeled “Number of tweets” and scaled linearly from 0 to over 400,000, marked with gridlines at intervals of 100,000. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of labels,” displays integer categories from 0 to 5. The chart shows that the category “Number of labels” equal to 1 has the highest bar, colored brown, reaching approximately 450,000 tweets; the category “Number of labels” equal to 2 has the second-highest bar, colored green, reaching approximately 410,000 tweets; the category “Number of labels” equal to 3 has a shorter bar, colored red, reaching approximately 100,000 tweets; and the categories “Number of labels” equal to 0 and 4 have very short bars, colored blue and purple respectively, each at approximately 5,000 tweets. The category “Number of labels” equal to 5 has no visible bar, indicating zero tweets. The bars are arranged in descending order of tweet count from left to right, with no visual emphasis such as shading or bolding applied to any specific bar.
